[h1]Original Review - August 2016[/h1]
This is a review by a non-crusader, non-hater, non-fanboy, who finished the game. 
I think you can consider me a hardcore fan of space, sandbox and open-world/exploration games.

Do not buy this UNLESS you're a hardcore fan of one of the genres. Do not buy this expecting good story, lore, or a good ending. Do not buy this expecting anything at all. Your best bet is to wait for a sale and a ton of patches.

The issue that makes No Man's Sky so hard to review for media outlets and the like, is that it takes a lot of hours for you to notice all of the shortcomings and problems with the game. It took me 10 hours to realize it wasn't as good as most people were saying, 20 hours to realize the game wouldn't evolve past the initial activities you perform at the first hours on the game, and 30 hours to realize that, gameplay-wise, the game feels like it was designed by game design students for some assignment.

I love procgen, I play a ton of indie and underground games which feature it - like Dwarf Fortress, my favorite game of all time - but the issue with procgen is that it will only provide infinite scenarios, objects, npcs, and things like that. Even though that can sound exciting, it won't take long for you to realize that what makes a procgen game amazing is the meaning it attributes to the stuff it randomly generates.

Example: in NMS, you have NPC ships and freighters flying around. They do nothing, they are nothing, they change nothing. They came from nowhere and aren't going anywhere. That Space-Station you just saw has no meaning and makes no difference, just like the last 70 you flew by on your way to the Galactic Core.

Sean Murray was my personal hero for these last 3 years, but he bit more than he could chew..and he probably can't even apologize for the game's flaws, issues and incompleteness because he has a contract with Sony. Hello Games hasn't even commented on the missing multiplayer component yet, wanna guess why?

This is Spore 2: Overloaded.

In Conclusion (or TL;DR): Unless you're a hardcore fan, or you have money lying around and absolutely nothing else to play, or if you just want a chill game that costs as much as an AAA game with less depth and worse game design than freeware games, be my guest. 
Everyone is streaming and talking about it, it's probably good...right?

This is not a $15 indie game. I've played those games, from Empyrion to Evochron, Starmade to Starbound and I like them for different reasons. Those are $15 experiences and can't be honestly compared to a game like No Man's Sky that on launch day became the most sophisticated procgen space sim available. While other games will feel barren (Elite: Dangerous, for example), NMS feels literally full of life, to the extent that had there been multiplayer support, I've already found planets discovered by other players in under 5 hours of play. As base-building and some other more customization features are still planned, maybe we'll eventually get the ability to stumble upon other players. For now, this is is an exceptional procgen exploration game for people like me who could play Proteus or Minecraft again and again just to look around. Even those games can't compare to the scale and variety of No Man's Sky out of the box.

Where the game may come off as a disappointment is in the repetitive scratch-ticket type gameplay where you look for technology upgrades and the necessary components to craft them. It's Zynga-style, MMO-grind microprogression that many games seem to include for people who want a constant fix. Your inventory is frustratingly small, though upgrading it is a clear motivation, and even your ability to see added variety will depend on how quickly you stumble upon the right items (though the game does include an Atlas helper who seems to point you in the right direction). It slows down getting the biggest and best equipment, though perhaps this sort of progression will be welcome 30 or so hours from now when procgen games seem to lose their novelty for awhile. The combat is fine, the ship navigation fluid enough to give you the rush of travelling through the atmosphere. Basebuilding will be welcome, but overall there's an acceptable amount of gameplay to go along with procgen that I think is worth the $60 all on its own.

As you have already heard and read from so many others, the game has turned around completely from its disastrous launch, and become a great game to play. Its newest update, "The Companions Update" allows you to tame most of the critters you find out in the procedurally generated universe to explore. You can have them lay eggs, alter the DNA of the un-born monster within, and tweak parts of your creature until you get it EXACTLY as you want it.
You can run the game as normal or in VR mode (provided you have the headset and computer capable of doing VR) and its quite the experience to BE the character as you go across flaming volcanic hellscapes, dive deep underwater in a ocean world, or slowly work your way through the halls of a derelict freighter lost in space as the tension builds as you hear something moving around the next corner . . .

All in all, if you like these kind of games, if it looks interesting to ya, I would recommend it! Spent 20hrs in game now, and it surely is repetitive, but towards a goal. So you slowly work your way towards upgrading your ship and inventory, your toughness to the environment and enemies, your ability to traverse the world/galaxy/universe so you can get to the centre of the universe.

There are little nuggets of story here and there but it is completely optional, and after a few hours you are given a choice which path you want to take, the quick way, the story way or your own way.

I would liken it to diablo in the way that you are doing the same shit over and over, but slowly you are getting pieces to get you there. Plus working towards chievos and exploring every corner of the planets is fun for completionists like myself.

DO NOT buy this game if you are not into this sort of thing. This is why the masses that purchased the game before actually knowing what the game is are complete and utter chumps. Why buy a game at full price if you have no idea what the game is... idiots.

I am loving it, and only like a small way from where I started in 20hrs due to me exploring a LOT. I can see many many more hours in this game :P



EDIT: Started again now many years after release, and the game feels incredible. So much more polished with clear goals to work towards and motivation at each point to make that next jump.
